name: Building Better Benchmarks for New Capabilities
gist: Papers design and construct new evaluation datasets for emerging abilities like agents solving real problems, code generation, scientific discovery, and handling specialized domains that weren't tested before.
explain: Every few months, AI models gain abilities no one tested before because machine learning keeps advancing and researchers build bigger, better-trained models. A model might suddenly be able to help you write a program, or reason through steps of a proof, or assist in scientific discovery, or handle medical or legal cases. Researchers who work on this subtheme build the tests for these brand-new skills, because old tests do not measure what these new abilities need measured. You have to invent a new way to measure something that barely existed in AI a year ago.

Why is this hard? Because new capability means new kinds of questions to ask. When researchers realized models could code, they had to design tests that checked not just whether code syntax is right, but whether it actually solves the problem, whether it is efficient, whether it handles edge cases. When models started helping in science—suggesting new molecules or designing proteins—researchers had to create benchmarks that capture what real scientific progress looks like, not just pattern matching. The papers in this group do that grunt work: they design, collect, and validate datasets that measure emerging skills honestly.

The approaches vary widely. Some papers gather real-world examples: actual coding tasks from open source repositories, real chemistry problems, actual cybersecurity scenarios. Others craft synthetic tests carefully designed to probe a specific weakness or skill, the way you might create math problems of increasing difficulty to see where a student starts to struggle. What ties them together is that they all build toward the same goal: once a benchmark exists and researchers agree it is trustworthy, everyone can use it to compare progress.

papers.title: A Benchmark for Deep Information Synthesis
papers.contribution: Demonstrates that state-of-the-art LLMs and agents achieve maximum F1 of 8.97, revealing that current agents struggle with hallucinations and reasoning over large information spaces.

papers.title: AstaBench: Rigorous Benchmarking of AI Agents with a Scientific Research Suite
papers.contribution: Provides rigorous principles and tooling for benchmarking agents across multiple scientific domains with better accounting for model cost and tool access confounders.

papers.title: Code2Bench: Scaling Source and Rigor for Dynamic Benchmark Construction
papers.contribution: Reveals fundamental performance gap where models excel at API application but struggle with algorithmic synthesis, uncovering illusion of correctness in simpler benchmarks.

papers.title: FinSearchComp: Towards a Realistic, Expert-Level Evaluation of Financial Search and Reasoning
papers.contribution: First open-source financial agent benchmark; Grok 4 approaches expert-level accuracy on global markets; web search and financial plugins significantly improve agent performance.

papers.title: From Assistant to Independent Developer — Are GPTs Ready for Software Development?
papers.contribution: First benchmark for end-to-end app development that evaluates whether LLMs can construct complete software systems with context-aware, robust code; enables reproducible assessment without human intervention.

papers.title: HardcoreLogic: Challenging Large Reasoning Models with Long-tail Logic Puzzle Games
papers.contribution: Reveals significant performance drops in Large Reasoning Models achieving top scores on existing benchmarks; exposes heavy reliance on memorized patterns and gaps in genuine reasoning.

papers.title: MMReD: a Cross-Modal Benchmark for Dense Context Reasoning
papers.contribution: Reveals consistent performance drops across all tested models as context length increases, with leading reasoning models achieving 0% accuracy on certain tasks at maximum context length of 128 observations.

papers.title: Orak: A Foundational Benchmark for Training and Evaluating LLM Agents on Diverse Video Games
papers.contribution: Establishes a comprehensive evaluation framework with leaderboards, battle arenas, and in-depth analysis of input modality and fine-tuning effects for versatile gaming agents.

papers.title: SOSBENCH: Benchmarking Safety Alignment on Scientific Knowledge
papers.contribution: Evaluates frontier models revealing alarmingly high harmful response rates (84.9% for Deepseek-R1, 50.3% for GPT-4.1) demonstrating significant safety alignment deficiencies.

papers.title: Scaling Up, Speeding Up: A Benchmark of Speculative Decoding for Efficient LLM Test-Time Scaling
papers.contribution: Simple n-gram methods effectively capture repetitive reasoning patterns, demonstrating value when integrated with model-based approaches for both repetitive and diverse reasoning.

papers.title: Terminal-Bench: Benchmarking Agents on Hard, Realistic Tasks in Command Line Interfaces
papers.contribution: Frontier models and agents score less than 50% on the benchmark; error analysis identifies areas for model and agent improvement.

papers.title: Towards Self-Evolving Agent Benchmarks : Validatable Agent Trajectory via Test-Time Exploration
papers.contribution: Demonstrates consistent task complexity enhancement on GAIA benchmark with improved correctness reliability through validatable reproducible trajectories, enabling self-evolving evaluation systems.

papers.title: VERINA: Benchmarking Verifiable Code Generation
papers.contribution: Reveals significant challenges in verifiable code generation, with the best model (OpenAI o3) achieving 72.6% code correctness, 52.3% specification soundness, and only 4.9% proof success rate.

papers.title: VideoPhy-2: A Challenging Action-Centric Physical Commonsense Evaluation in Video Generation
papers.contribution: Reveals major shortcomings with best models achieving only 47.7% joint performance on hard subset; models struggle particularly with conservation laws like mass and momentum.

papers.title: $\tau$-Knowledge: Evaluating Conversational Agents over Unstructured Knowledge
papers.contribution: Even frontier models achieve only ~25.5% pass rate, revealing challenges in dense knowledge retrieval and complex policy reasoning.

papers.title: A Benchmark and Framework for Evaluating Next Action Predictions in Spreadsheets
papers.contribution: Provides foundation for spreadsheet action prediction with multiple baselines and analysis of action properties, user profiles, triggers, and context effects.

papers.title: ACADREASON: Exploring the Limits of Reasoning Models with Academic Research Problems
papers.contribution: Most LLMs scored below 20 points with GPT-5 achieving only 16 points and best agents under 40 points, demonstrating significant capability gaps.

papers.title: ACPBench Hard: Unrestrained Reasoning about Action, Change, and Planning
papers.contribution: Benchmark testing reveals that even the largest frontier models score below 65%, with the top model achieving only 8-51% accuracy, showing that current LLMs have a long way to go for reliable reasoning about planning.

papers.title: ASyMOB: Algebraic Symbolic Mathematical Operations Benchmark
papers.contribution: Reveal that most models' performance collapses under minor perturbations while top systems show regime shift in robustness, and identify cases where LLMs succeed while CAS fails.

papers.title: AetherCode: Evaluating LLMs’ Ability to Win In Premier Programming Competitions
papers.contribution: Provides a more faithful measure of LLM reasoning capabilities than existing benchmarks with comprehensive, expert-validated evaluation.

papers.title: AgentSuite: Toward More Reliable Agent Evaluation with a Component-Based Benchmark Auditing Pipeline
papers.contribution: Achieves F1 scores 0.791-0.874 aligning with expert judgments and identifies missed issues in tau-bench; released AgentSuite platform.

papers.title: AlgoVeri: An Aligned Benchmark for Verified Code Generation on Classical Algorithms
papers.contribution: Demonstrate that frontier models achieve 40.3% in Dafny but performance collapses to 24.7% in Verus and 7.8% in Lean, revealing systems-level and proof-construction barriers.

papers.title: AlphaBench: Benchmarking Large Language Models in Formulaic Alpha Factor Mining
papers.contribution: The benchmark reveals that LLMs have strong potential in automating factor mining while facing challenges in robustness, search efficiency, and practical usability.

papers.title: Benchmarking World-Model Learning with Environment-Level Queries
papers.contribution: Experiments with 517 humans and five frontier models show substantial human advantage, attributed to differences in exploration and belief updating capabilities.

papers.title: CMPhysBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models in Condensed Matter Physics
papers.contribution: Best models reach only 36 average SEED score and 29% accuracy, demonstrating substantial capability gaps in practical physics domain knowledge.

papers.title: CUARewardBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Reward Models for Computer-Using Agents
papers.contribution: Reveals critical limitations in current CUA reward models and shows general VLMs outperform specialized CUA models.

papers.title: CentaurEval: Benchmarking Human-in-the-Loop Value in Agentic Coding
papers.contribution: While LLMs/humans alone achieve poor rates (0.67% and 18.89%), human-AI collaboration improves to 31.11% under strategic intervention.

papers.title: Charts Are Not Images: On the Challenges of Scientific Chart Editing
papers.contribution: Evaluation of state-of-the-art models reveals poor performance on scientific figures and that traditional metrics like SSIM and PSNR have limitations in capturing semantic correctness of edits.

papers.title: CodeClash: Benchmarking Goal-Oriented Software Engineering
papers.contribution: Reveals diverse development styles and fundamental limitations in strategic reasoning; top models lose every round to expert humans.

papers.title: Constantly Improving Image Models Need Constantly Improving Benchmarks
papers.contribution: Curates 35,000 prompts revealing complex tasks absent from existing benchmarks and surfaces community feedback for metric design.

papers.title: Constructing Industrial-Scale Optimization Modeling Benchmark
papers.contribution: Provides 223 industrial-scale benchmarks revealing substantial performance degradation in systems that perform well on existing benchmarks.

papers.title: CrossPL: Systematic Evaluation of Large Language Models for Cross Programming Language Interoperating Code Generation
papers.contribution: Evaluates 20 state-of-the-art LLMs, revealing clear limitations with best model achieving only 19.5% Pass@1 on FFI subset, underscoring urgent need to improve cross-language code generation.

papers.title: Culture In a Frame: C$^3$B as a Comic-Based Benchmark for Multimodal Culturally Awareness
papers.contribution: Evaluations on 11 open-source MLLMs reveal significant performance gap between MLLMs and human performance, demonstrating that C³B poses substantial challenges for current models.

papers.title: DARE-bench: Evaluating Modeling and Instruction Fidelity of LLMs in Data Science
papers.contribution: Supervised fine-tuning boosts Qwen3-32B accuracy 1.83x and reinforcement learning boosts Qwen3-4B accuracy more than 8x, demonstrating DARE-bench's value for training and evaluation.

papers.title: DHG-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Deep Hypergraph Learning
papers.contribution: Provides comprehensive benchmark revealing strengths and limitations of existing algorithms and offers an easy-to-use library for reproducible HNN research.

papers.title: DLEBench: Evaluating Small-scale Object Editing Ability for Instruction-based Image Editing Model
papers.contribution: Reveals significant performance gaps in small-scale object editing across 10 IIEMs, highlighting need for specialized benchmarks.

papers.title: DRIFT-BENCH: Diagnosing CoopeRative Breakdowns in LLM Agents under Input Faults via Multi-Turn Interaction
papers.contribution: Experiments show substantial performance drops under input faults with varying clarification effectiveness across personas and fault types, connecting clarification studies with agent benchmarking.

papers.title: DeepMath-103K: A Large-Scale, Challenging, Decontaminated, and Verifiable Mathematical Dataset for Advancing Reasoning
papers.contribution: Models trained on DeepMath-103K achieve leading results on mathematical benchmarks and demonstrate generalization to biology, physics, and chemistry.

papers.title: DetailMaster: Can Your Text-to-Image Model Handle Long Prompts?
papers.contribution: Evaluations reveal critical limitations: weak encoders struggle with syntactic dependencies while diffusion models suffer attribute leakage under detail-intensive conditions; high-fidelity generation requires both expanded prompt limits and long-prompt trainin

papers.title: Do LLMs Forget What They Should? Evaluating In-Context Forgetting in Large Language Models
papers.contribution: Advanced LLMs perform well without interference but struggle significantly when interference is present, with stronger memory not translating to stronger in-context forgetting capacity and context length having differential effects across scenarios.

papers.title: EDINET-Bench: Evaluating LLMs on Complex Financial Tasks using Japanese Financial Statements
papers.contribution: Demonstrates that state-of-the-art LLMs barely outperform logistic regression on fraud detection and earnings forecasting, highlighting need for richer scaffolding and task-specific reasoning.

papers.title: EXP-Bench: Can AI Conduct AI Research Experiments?
papers.contribution: Evaluations reveal that while individual aspects reach 20-35% accuracy, complete executable experiment success rate is 0.5%, identifying critical bottlenecks for future AI research agents.

papers.title: EarthSE: A Benchmark Evaluating Earth Scientific Exploration Capability for Large Language Models
papers.contribution: Extensive experiments on 11 leading LLMs reveal significant limitations across different domains and tasks, highlighting substantial room for improvement in scientific exploration capabilities.

papers.title: Easier Painting Than Thinking: Can Text-to-Image Models Set the Stage, but Not Direct the Play?
papers.contribution: T2I-CoReBench provides comprehensive and fine-grained evaluation of composition and reasoning capabilities across diverse T2I models.

papers.title: EditBench: Evaluating LLM Abilities to Perform Real-World Instructed Code Edits
papers.contribution: EditBench shows that only 3 of 40 diverse LLMs score over 60%, revealing significant variation across instruction categories and demonstrating that contextual information affects task success by up to 11%.

papers.title: Evaluating Memory in LLM Agents via Incremental Multi-Turn Interactions
papers.contribution: Provides comprehensive testbed for memory agents across four competencies with multi-turn interactive format reflecting agent behavior.

papers.title: Evolution of Benchmark: Black-Box Optimization Benchmark Design through Large Language Model
papers.contribution: EoB provides a competitive automated benchmark designer applicable to benchmarking algorithms, training learning-assisted BBO solvers, and extending proxies for real-world problems.

papers.title: Exploring Real-Time Super-Resolution: Benchmarking and Fine-Tuning for Streaming Content
papers.contribution: Demonstrates fine-tuning on StreamSR yields significant performance gains generalizing across standard benchmarks for streaming super-resolution.

papers.title: ForestPersons: A Large-Scale Dataset for Under-Canopy Missing Person Detection
papers.contribution: Demonstrates standard object detection models trained on prior datasets show limited performance, indicating a gap requiring specialized benchmarks for forest SAR.

papers.title: FutureX: An Advanced Live Benchmark for LLM Agents in Future Prediction
papers.contribution: Establishes largest and most diverse live benchmark for future prediction with contamination-free evaluation through automated pipeline.

papers.title: GENEB: Why Genomic Models Are Hard to Compare
papers.contribution: Reveals aggregate leaderboards are unstable with model rankings varying sharply across categories; scale provides modest inconsistent gains; architectural and pretraining alignment often outweigh parameter count.

papers.title: Gaia2: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Dynamic and Asynchronous Environments
papers.contribution: Gaia2 evaluation reveals trade-offs between reasoning, efficiency, and robustness across state-of-the-art models: GPT-5 reaches 42% pass@1 on overall performance but fails on time-sensitive tasks, while Kimi-K2 leads open-source at 21%.

papers.title: GhostEI-Bench: Do Mobile Agent Resilience to Environmental Injection in Dynamic On-Device Environments?
papers.contribution: Comprehensive evaluation reveals state-of-the-art agents' profound vulnerability to environmental injection, identifies precise failure points in perception, recognition, or reasoning.

papers.title: Gistify: Codebase-Level Understanding via Runtime Execution
papers.contribution: Introduces a benchmark requiring structural codebase understanding, accurate execution flow modeling, and large code patch generation; shows current state-of-the-art models struggle with complex traces.

papers.title: GraphOmni: A Comprehensive and Extensible Benchmark Framework for Large Language Models on Graph-theoretic Tasks
papers.contribution: Reveals closed-source models like Claude-3.5 lead overall but leave headroom; reduces evaluation cost by 75% via adaptive factor selection while retaining accuracy.

papers.title: HeurekaBench: A Benchmarking Framework for AI Co-scientist
papers.contribution: Enables quantitative end-to-end evaluation of scientific agents; shows adding a critic module improves ill-formed responses by up to 22%, setting a path toward rigorous agentic system evaluation.

papers.title: HiPhO: How Far Are (M)LLMs from Humans in the Latest High School Physics Olympiad Benchmark?
papers.contribution: Evaluation of 30 LLMs shows most open-source models remain below bronze level, while closed-source ones achieve 6-13 gold medals, revealing substantial gaps to top human contestants.

papers.title: How Many Code and Test Cases Are Enough? Evaluating Test Cases Generation from a Binary-Matrix Perspective
papers.contribution: Introduces novel framework using matrix rank for efficient benchmark construction that maximizes internal diversity and identifies minimal sufficient wrong codes and test cases.

papers.title: InclusiveVidPose: Bridging the Pose Estimation Gap for Individuals with Limb Deficiencies in Video-Based Motion
papers.contribution: Provides comprehensive annotations with 400+ individuals and introduces Limb-specific Confidence Consistency metric highlighting limitations of existing HPE models.

papers.title: InfoMosaic-Bench: Evaluating Multi-Source Information Seeking in Tool-Augmented Agents
papers.contribution: Reveals that GPT-5 achieves only 38.2% accuracy with web alone, domain tools provide selective benefits, and 22.4% of failures stem from incorrect tool usage.

papers.title: InnovatorBench: Evaluating Agents’ Ability to Conduct Innovative AI Research
papers.contribution: Frontier models achieve promise on code-driven tasks but struggle with algorithm-related tasks and long-horizon decision making, requiring over 11 hours to reach best performance.

papers.title: InteractScience: Programmatic and Visually-Grounded Evaluation of Interactive Scientific Demonstration Code Generation
papers.contribution: First benchmark dedicated to interactive scientific application generation reveals critical gaps in grounding scientific reasoning within interactive interfaces.

papers.title: Inverse IFEval: Can LLMs Unlearn Stubborn Training Conventions to Follow Real Instructions?
papers.contribution: Empirical results on 1012 high-quality Chinese and English questions across 23 domains demonstrate necessity of addressing cognitive inertia in alignment.

papers.title: Is Your Paper Being Reviewed by an LLM? Benchmarking AI Text Detection in Peer Review
papers.contribution: The evaluation reveals the difficulty of identifying AI-generated peer reviews at the individual level, highlighting the urgent need for better detection tools.

papers.title: It's TIME: Towards the Next Generation of Time Series Forecasting Benchmarks
papers.contribution: TIME enables strict zero-shot TSFM evaluation free from data leakage and provides a multi-granular leaderboard evaluating 12 TSFMs with generalizable insights.

papers.title: LFQA-E: Carefully Benchmarking Long-form QA Evaluation
papers.contribution: Results demonstrate that none of the existing automatic metrics perform comparably to human judgments, providing detailed failure case analysis and generalization capacity insights.

papers.title: Leaderboard Incentives: Model Rankings under Strategic Post-Training
papers.contribution: Demonstrates benchmarks need not induce bad incentives and provides principled evaluation protocols that rank models by latent quality.

papers.title: LiveOIBench: Can Large Language Models Outperform Human Contestants in Informatics Olympiads?
papers.contribution: Enable direct comparison of 34 LLMs to elite human contestants, finding GPT-5 achieves 81.76th percentile while GPT-OSS-120B reaches 60th percentile.

papers.title: LoCoT2V-Bench: Benchmarking Long-Form and Complex Text-to-Video Generation
papers.contribution: Experiments on 17 LVG models reveal strong perceptual quality but weak fine-grained text-video alignment and character consistency, identifying key challenges.

papers.title: MATH-Beyond: A Benchmark for RL to Expand Beyond the Base Model
papers.contribution: Shows that existing RL approaches perform poorly on harder instances, catalyzing exploration-driven methods that elicit deeper reasoning beyond base model capabilities.

papers.title: MCPMark: A Benchmark for Stress-Testing Realistic and Comprehensive MCP Use
papers.contribution: Best models reach only 52.56% pass@1 on MCPMark, exposing significant weaknesses in current LLMs despite high performance on simpler benchmarks.

papers.title: MMR-Life: Piecing Together Real-life Scenes for Multimodal Multi-image Reasoning
papers.contribution: Even top models like GPT-5 achieve only 58% accuracy, revealing substantial challenge and considerable performance variance across reasoning types, establishing a foundation for evaluating next-generation multimodal reasoning systems.

papers.title: MMSU: A Massive Multi-task Spoken Language Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark
papers.contribution: Evaluates 22 advanced SpeechLLMs revealing substantial room for improvement, establishing new standards for comprehensive speech language understanding assessment.

papers.title: MathNet: A Global Multimodal Benchmark for Mathematical Reasoning and Retrieval
papers.contribution: MathNet is the largest high-quality Olympiad dataset with the first retrieval benchmark for problem equivalence; state-of-the-art reasoning models achieve 76.8% (GPT-5) and 46.8% (Claude 4.5 Opus), showing significant remaining challenges.

papers.title: MedAgentGym: A Scalable Agentic Training Environment for Code-Centric Reasoning in Biomedical Data Science
papers.contribution: Med-Copilot achieves +43.02% (offline) and +45.28% (online) RL gains, establishing a cost-effective, privacy-preserving alternative competitive with proprietary LLMs.

papers.title: MemoryBench: A Benchmark for Memory and Continual Learning in LLM Systems
papers.contribution: Introduce MemoryBench showing that state-of-the-art baselines achieve far-from-satisfying effectiveness and efficiency on continual learning from user feedback.

papers.title: MoReBench: Evaluating Procedural and Pluralistic Moral Reasoning in Language Models, More than Outcomes
papers.contribution: Shows that scaling laws from math/code reasoning fail to predict moral reasoning abilities, and reveals model partiality toward specific ethics frameworks.

papers.title: Multi-LCB: Extending LiveCodeBench to Multiple Programming Languages
papers.contribution: Uncovers Python overfitting, language-specific contamination, and substantial multilingual performance disparities in evaluated LLMs.

papers.title: NC-Bench and NCfold: A Benchmark and Closed-Loop Framework for RNA Non-Canonical Base-Pair Prediction
papers.contribution: NCfold outperforms existing methods on NC-Bench, with zero-shot studies confirming effectiveness and establishing a foundation for non-canonical base-pair prediction.

papers.title: NarrLV: Towards a Comprehensive Narrative-Centric Evaluation for Long Video Generation
papers.contribution: First comprehensive benchmark for evaluating narrative expression capabilities of long video generation models with automatic prompt generation and evaluation framework.

papers.title: Not Search, But Scan: Benchmarking MLLMs on Scan-Oriented Academic Paper Reasoning
papers.contribution: Assessment of 15 models reveals systematic deficiencies on scan-oriented tasks, with retrieval-augmented generation yielding no significant improvements.

papers.title: NurValues: Real-World Nursing Values Evaluation for Large Language Models in Clinical Context
papers.contribution: Evaluates 23 SoTA LLMs revealing general LLMs outperform medical ones, and Justice dimension is hardest for value alignment.

papers.title: OPT-Engine: Benchmarking the Limits of LLMs in Optimization Modeling via Complexity Scaling
papers.contribution: Identifies constraint formulation as the primary bottleneck in current LLM approaches and provides structured roadmap for developing next-generation LLMs for optimization modeling.

papers.title: OmniCVR: A Benchmark for Omni-Composed Video Retrieval with Vision, Audio, and Text
papers.contribution: Establishes OmniCVR large-scale benchmark and AudioVLM2Vec achieves state-of-the-art, revealing fundamental audio reasoning limitations in current multimodal systems.

papers.title: On the Eligibility of LLMs for Counterfactual Reasoning: A Decompositional Study
papers.contribution: The framework characterizes LLM behavior at each decompositional stage and identifies how modality type and intermediate reasoning influence counterfactual reasoning performance.

papers.title: OpenMAG: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Multimodal-Attributed Graph
papers.contribution: Derives 14 fundamental insights into MAG learning to guide future advancements through systematic assessment.

papers.title: OpenPros: A Large-Scale Dataset for Limited View Prostate Ultrasound Computed Tomography
papers.contribution: Benchmarking shows deep learning methods significantly outperform physics-based algorithms in inference efficiency and reconstruction accuracy on limited-angle USCT.

papers.title: OptimalThinkingBench: Evaluating Over and Underthinking in LLMs
papers.contribution: Shows that no model optimally thinks on the benchmark; thinking models often waste hundreds of tokens on simplest queries without improvement, highlighting the need for better unified models.

papers.title: OrchestrationBench: LLM-Driven Agentic Planning and Tool Use in Multi-Domain Scenarios
papers.contribution: Reveals that function calling is consistent across models while planning varies substantially, with extensive experiments on state-of-the-art models.

papers.title: Outrunning LLM Cutoffs: A Live Kernel Crash Resolution Benchmark for All
papers.contribution: Curates 534 Linux kernel bugs; shows agents achieve 25% higher patch rate on pre-cutoff bugs versus newer bugs, resolving 74% on first attempt but only 20% closely match developer fixes; feedback exposure improves resolution by 29%.

papers.title: PerSpectra: A Scalable and Configurable Pluralist Benchmark of Perspectives from Arguments
papers.contribution: The benchmark enables three tasks (opinion counting, opinion matching, polarity check) and reveals systematic failures of state-of-the-art models in handling pluralism, establishing a foundation for evaluating LLMs on perspective diversity.

papers.title: PlotCraft: Pushing the Limits of LLMs for Complex and Interactive Data Visualization
papers.contribution: PlotCraftor achieves performance comparable to leading proprietary approaches, with over 50% improvement on hard tasks.

papers.title: PoseX: AI Defeats Physics-based Methods on Protein Ligand Cross-Docking
papers.contribution: PoseX reveals that AI-based approaches consistently outperform physics-based methods overall, and combining AI modeling with physics-based post-processing achieves excellent performance.

papers.title: Procedural Generation Of Algorithm Discovery Tasks in Machine Learning
papers.contribution: Enables large-scale optimization of algorithm discovery agents and exposes failure modes invisible at toy scale.

papers.title: QuArch: A Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Reasoning in Computer Architecture
papers.contribution: Frontier model accuracies vary widely (34% to 73%) on advanced questions; fine-tuning on QuArch improves memory hierarchy design task performance up to 1.99x.

papers.title: Quantifying the Generalization Gap in Seizure Detection: A Large-Scale Empirical Benchmark via the SzCORE Challenge
papers.contribution: Reveals top F1 score of 32% highlighting persistent difficulty of seizure detection, identifies discordance between peak performance and population-level stability, and uncovers key failure modes.

papers.title: RECODE: A Benchmark for Research Code DEvelopment with Interactive Human Feedback
papers.contribution: Experiments on GPT-5, Claude-Sonnet-4, DeepSeek-V3.1, and Gemini 2.5 show substantial performance gains with richer feedback, establishing a foundation for feedback-driven LLM agents in scientific research.

papers.title: RF-MatID: Dataset and Benchmark for Radio Frequency Material Identification
papers.contribution: RF-MatID establishes multi-setting benchmarks evaluating deep learning models and assessing robustness under cross-angle and cross-distance shifts for real-world RF-based material identification.

papers.title: Referring Layer Decomposition
papers.contribution: Enables prompt-conditioned layer decomposition achieving high visual fidelity with strong zero-shot generalization on 1.11M image-layer-prompt triplets.

papers.title: RefineBench: Evaluating Refinement Capability in Language Models
papers.contribution: Shows frontier LMs achieve modest baseline self-refinement scores (Gemini 2.5 Pro 31.1%, GPT-4.1 23.4%) but leverage targeted feedback for near-perfect refinement within five turns.

papers.title: RobustSpring: Benchmarking Robustness to Image Corruptions for Optical Flow, Scene Flow and Stereo
papers.contribution: Introduces comprehensive corruption robustness metric and dataset revealing wide variation in model robustness across corruption types, with evidence that RobustSpring indicates real-world resilience.

papers.title: SCOPE and SCION: A Benchmark and an Auditable Reference Pipeline for Schema Induction and Fusion from Text
papers.contribution: SCION-lite attains highest F1 among released baselines under multiple schema-graph metrics; release includes evidence-linked outputs and code.

papers.title: SPEED-Bench: A Unified and Diverse Benchmark for Speculative Decoding
papers.contribution: Reveals how synthetic inputs overestimate real throughput, identifies batch-size dependent optimal draft lengths, and analyzes vocabulary pruning biases.

papers.title: SWE-Compass: Towards Unified Evaluation of Agentic Coding Abilities for Large Language Models
papers.contribution: Reveals clear hierarchy of difficulty across task types and languages, providing rigorous foundation for diagnosing agentic coding capabilities across diverse real-world programming tasks.

papers.title: SWINGARENA: Adversarial Programming Arena for Long-context GitHub Issue Solving
papers.contribution: Presents a scalable methodology for evaluating LLMs in realistic CI-driven software development with over 400 real-world GitHub issues.

papers.title: Sci2Pol: Evaluating and Fine-tuning LLMs on Scientific-to-Policy Brief Generation
papers.contribution: After fine-tuning on our curated 639-example corpus, Gemma-27B surpasses GPT-4o and DeepSeek-V3 on the benchmark.

papers.title: SciVideoBench: Benchmarking Scientific Video Reasoning in Large Multimodal Models
papers.contribution: Reveals significant performance deficits in state-of-the-art LMMs including Gemini 2.5 Pro and Qwen2.5-VL, indicating substantial room for advancement.

papers.title: ScienceBoard: Evaluating Multimodal Autonomous Agents in Realistic Scientific Workflows
papers.contribution: Evaluation shows that state-of-the-art agents like GPT-4o and Claude 3.7 only achieve 15% overall success rate, revealing fundamental limitations in complex workflow assistance.

papers.title: SealQA: Raising the Bar for Reasoning in Search-Augmented Language Models
papers.contribution: Even frontier reasoning models like GPT-5 achieve only 43.2% on SEAL-0, and test-time compute increases often plateau or decline; models struggle with document selection in long-context scenarios.

papers.title: SeisMark: A Large-Scale Open Benchmark for Robust 3D Seismic Fault Detection
papers.contribution: Acts as rigorous discriminator distinguishing robust modern architecture from legacy models; establishes verifiable standard for trustworthy safety-critical subsurface AI.

papers.title: StoryAlign: Evaluating and Training Reward Models for Story Generation
papers.contribution: StoryReward achieves state-of-the-art performance on StoryRMB, outperforming much larger models, and performs well in downstream best-of-n story selection applications.

papers.title: Strategic Navigation or Stochastic Search? How Agents and Humans Reason Over Document Collections
papers.contribution: The benchmark shows best agents match human accuracy but on different questions, fail to close a 20% gap to oracle performance, and persist in unproductive loops.

papers.title: Synthesizing Multimodal Geometry Datasets from Scratch and Enabling Visual Alignment via Plotting Code
papers.contribution: GeoCode demonstrates higher structural complexity than existing benchmarks while maintaining mathematical correctness, showing consistent improvements on multiple geometry benchmarks.

papers.title: Synthetic History: Evaluating Visual Representations of the Past in Diffusion Models
papers.contribution: Findings reveal systematic inaccuracies including unstated stylistic cues that stereotype past eras, anachronisms such as modern artifacts in pre-modern contexts, and unrealistic demographic patterns.

papers.title: TSM-Bench: Detecting LLM-Generated Text in Real-World Wikipedia Editing Practices
papers.contribution: Average detection accuracy drops 10-40% compared to prior benchmarks; fine-tuning on task-specific data enables cross-domain generalization but not vice versa.

papers.title: Talk, Evaluate, Diagnose: User-aware Agent Evaluation with Automated Error Analysis
papers.contribution: Reveals insights on agent performance across models and user expertise levels, providing actionable feedback for improvement.

papers.title: The Open Proof Corpus: A Large-Scale Study of LLM-Generated Mathematical Proofs
papers.contribution: The OPC allows finetuning an 8B model to match Gemini-2.5-Pro and perform close to GPT-5 on proof correctness evaluation.

papers.title: Thinking in Structures: Evaluating Spatial Intelligence in Constraint-Governed Spaces
papers.contribution: Reveals large human-model gap: best open-source model 22.2%, strongest closed-source 33.6%, humans 91.6%, showing fundamental spatial-understanding limitations with minimal gains from chain-of-thought.

papers.title: TimeSeriesExamAgent: Creating TimeSeries Reasoning Benchmarks at Scale
papers.contribution: The framework generates diverse benchmarks with quality comparable to manual curation while revealing that LLMs have limited performance in abstract reasoning and domain-specific applications.

papers.title: TimeSpot: Benchmarking Geo-Temporal Understanding in Vision–Language Models in Real-World Settings
papers.contribution: Evaluations show low performance in temporal inference; supervised fine-tuning yields improvements but remains insufficient.

papers.title: Towards Multimodal Data-Driven Scientific Discovery Powered by LLM Agents
papers.contribution: Only 48.94% accuracy achieved by strongest agents with over 60% failures from cross-modal alignment, establishing rigorous testbed for advancing LLM agents.

papers.title: Towards a Science of AI Agent Reliability
papers.contribution: Recent capability gains yield only small improvements in reliability across 15 models on two benchmarks, exposing persistent limitations beyond what single-metric evaluations reveal.

papers.title: TritonGym: A Benchmark for Agentic LLM Workflows in Triton GPU Code Generation
papers.contribution: TritonGym spans maintained operators, community samples, and out-of-distribution tasks, enabling fair comparison and facilitating progress on agentic GPU-code systems.

papers.title: Unison: Benchmarking Unified Multimodal Models via Synergistic Understanding and Generation
papers.contribution: Uncovers critical limitations in current unified systems through holistic evaluation and provides Unison-Judge for human-aligned assessment.

papers.title: VLM-SubtleBench: How Far Are VLMs from Human-Level Subtle Comparative Reasoning?
papers.contribution: Reveals systematic gaps between VLM and human performance on subtle differences, establishing foundation for advancing toward human-level comparative reasoning.

papers.title: VPD-100K: Towards Generalizable and Fine-grained Visual Privacy Protection
papers.contribution: Large-scale fine-grained Visual Privacy Dataset featuring long-tailed distributions and small object scales; provides frequency-domain attention fusion and adaptive spectral gating for sensitive information detection.

papers.title: VeriEquivBench: An Equivalence Score for Ground-Truth-Free Evaluation of Formally Verifiable Code
papers.contribution: VeriEquivBench with 2,389 complex algorithmic problems reveals that formally verifiable code generation remains profoundly challenging for state-of-the-art LLMs.

papers.title: VerifyBench: Benchmarking Reference-based Reward Systems for Large Language Models
papers.contribution: Establishes standardized framework for evaluating verification systems; reveals all current systems have substantial room for improvement on challenging instances.

papers.title: WebDS: An End-to-End Benchmark for Web-based Data Science
papers.contribution: Reveals significant performance gaps with current SOTA LLM agents (15% completion vs 80% on Web Voyager) and identifies new failure modes like poor grounding and repetitive behavior.

papers.title: When to use Graphs in RAG: A Comprehensive Analysis for Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation
papers.contribution: Systematically investigates when GraphRAG surpasses vanilla RAG and provides practical guidelines; evaluates entire pipeline from graph construction to generation.

papers.title: Why We Need New Benchmarks for Local Intrinsic Dimension Estimation
papers.contribution: Identifies critical limitations of state-of-the-art LID methods and new directions for future development through comparative analysis.

papers.title: World2Minecraft: Occupancy-Driven simulated scenes Construction
papers.contribution: Introduces MinecraftOcc dataset with 100,165 images from 156 detailed indoor scenes; demonstrates dataset improves occupancy prediction and provides customizable embodied AI research platform.

papers.title: iWorld-Bench: A Benchmark for Interactive World Models with a Unified Action Generation Framework
papers.contribution: Evaluates 14 world models identifying key limitations, provides public leaderboard and insights for future research.
